Title: July 20, 2023 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
Overview: The Council heard extensive public comment on smoke-free laws, cannabis hospitality, minimum wage, and airport issues. It unanimously passed the consent agenda, including three alternative versions of a sales tax extension ballot measure for first reading. Council took no action to add marijuana hospitality establishments to the work plan or to fund engagement, leaving that question to a future Council, and it then discussed safety on Boulder Creek after recent drownings.

Topic1.Title: Public Comment on Smoke-Free Laws and Cannabis Hospitality
Topic1.Summary: Residents, representatives of public health groups, and industry advocates spoke during open comment. Public health speakers urged the Council to keep smoke-free air protections and opposed allowing smoking or vaping in public places, including cannabis. Chamber of Commerce and cannabis industry speakers supported marijuana hospitality establishments as a way to regulate consumption and support business. Several speakers also raised concerns about drug harm reduction services and public drug use downtown.

Topic2.Title: Minimum Wage Public Comment
Topic2.Summary: Union members and residents urged the Council to join Boulder County in raising the local minimum wage, with some asking for implementation in 2024 rather than 2025. Speakers framed the wage increase as an economic security and housing affordability measure. The Chamber of Commerce asked for a deliberate process that accounts for small nonprofit budgets. A staff update later noted that nearby communities preferred 2025 implementation.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Sales Tax Ballot Measures
Topic3.Summary: The Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3H unanimously. The agenda included three alternative versions of a ballot measure to extend the 0.15 percent sales tax that would otherwise expire at the end of next year. Council planned to pass all three on first reading and hold a public hearing on August 3 before narrowing the options. Another consent item allowed land use approvals to remain valid for three years instead of one.

Topic4.Title: Marijuana Hospitality Establishments Direction
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented Cannabis Licensing Advisory Board recommendations on opting in to state law allowing marijuana hospitality establishments. Staff asked whether Council wanted this added to a future work plan and what level of public engagement to pursue. Most Council members said the item should not be added this year because of staff capacity and the timing near the end of the term. Council opted not to direct a consultant or engagement now and suggested the next Council consider the item at its retreat.

Topic5.Title: Boulder Creek Public Safety After Drownings
Topic5.Summary: Fire Chief Calderazzo and Parks and Recreation Director Rhodes described emergency response to recent Boulder Creek drownings and current closure protocols tied to county flow thresholds of 700 cubic feet per second. Proposed measures include throw-line stations, temporary and permanent signage by April 2024, and a Creek Management Plan. Council discussed requiring personal flotation devices, expanding swim lessons through financial aid, and coordinating with the sheriff and the school district. Council members expressed condolences to the families affected.
